newsitem.title: USA: US, EU meat talks seen moving next week to Brussels.
newsitem.headline: US, EU meat talks seen moving next week to Brussels.

text.p: Bilateral talks between the United States and the European Union on meat import inspection regulations are expected to continue next week in Brussels, an official familiar with the ongoing talks said Wednesday.
"The USDA folks are going to Brussels (next) Tuesday," said the official who did not want to be identified. "Don't write the talks off after tomorrow."

U.S. and EU officials have been meeting this week in Washington in a last-ditch effort to reach agreement in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks and avoid a nasty trade war that could disrupt the commerce of hundreds of dollars worth of poultry and meat products.

The officials met until 2100 EDT Tuesday night and were expected to meet into the Wednesday evening. More talks are likely Thursday morning before EU officials are scheduled to depart later in the day.
U.S. and EU sources said Wednesday that it did not appear that much progress has been made in this week's talks. Both sides are taking a hard line, they said.

Washington and Brussels are trying to reach an agreement in the talks which ended last week without resolution by an April 1 deadline. An agreement would allow each side to import meat and poultry from the other even if inpsection methods differ.

The unsuccessful conclusion of last week's talks prompted moves on both sides of the Atlantic to restrict trade, and negotiators are now scrambling to reach a deal before April 15, when the United States has threatened to remove more than 100 EU meat and poultry processing plants from its list of approved exporters.
